header.running_head: The Sahabah (RA) Exercise Patience with Illness

blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) replied, "It is He (Allaah) Who has made me lay here (with this illness)."[^1]
The Patience Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) and his Family Exercised During the Plague

Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Ghanam reports that when the plague struck Shaam, Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) announced, "This plague is a punishment, so flee from it to the valleys and ravines." When news of this statement reached Hadhrat Shurahbeel bin Hasanah (RA), he became incensed and said, "Amr bin Al Aas is wrong! I was a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ at a time when Amr was more astray than the camel his family owns. This plague is the du'aa of your Nabi ﷺ[^2], the mercy of your Rabb[^3] and the way in which many pious people lost their lives in the past."
When this news reached Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA), he prayed, "O Allaah! Grant the family of Mu'aadh their share in full." His two daughters then passed away in the plague and his son Abdur Rahmaan was also afflicted. Advising his son, Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) recited the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: اَلْحَقُّ مِنْ رَّبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُوْنَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِيْنَ
blocks.text: The truth is from your Rabb so never be among those who doubt.
To this, his son replied with the following verse of the Qur'aan:

blocks.arabic_text: سَتَجِدُنِيْ إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ مِنَ الصّٰبِرِيْنَ
blocks.text: If Allaah wills, you will soon find me to be among the patient ones.

The plague then struck Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) himself (and it showed up first) on the back of his hand. "This," Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) said, "is more beloved to me than red camels." When he saw a man weeping beside him, he asked, "What makes you weep?" The man replied, "I am crying over the knowledge I used to gain from you (which I shall no longer be gaining after your demise)." "Do not cry," Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) consoled him, "because although Hadhrat Ibraheem (AS) was in a place where there was no knowledge to be learnt, Allaah gave him the knowledge. After I die, seek knowledge from four men (viz.) Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA), Salmaan (RA) and Abu Dardaa (RA)."[^4]

Another narration states that Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA), Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA), Hadhrat Shurahbeel bin Hasanah (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Maalik Ash'ari (RA) were all struck by the plague on the same day. Hadhrat
Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.141), Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in his Zuhd and Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.34), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.153).
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.218). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.7 Pg.118) has reported a similar narration.
Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa to Allaah to accord the status of a martyr to any person of his Ummah who died in a plague.
Someone who dies in a plague is a martyr in the sight of Allaah.
